root_cause.text: The kprobes ftrace-disarm path in `__disarm_kprobe_ftrace()` could still invoke ftrace unregister/disarm operations even after `ftrace_kill()` had set `kprobe_ftrace_disabled`, so module unload/reload later dereferenced invalid ftrace state and crashed in `kprobes_module_callback()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says “the kprobe on ftrace does not correctly handles the `kprobe_ftrace_disabled` flag set by `ftrace_kill()`,” and the patch adds an early return in `__disarm_kprobe_ftrace()` when `kprobe_ftrace_disabled` is true, with the comment “Now ftrace is disabled forever, disarm is already done.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The kprobes ftrace-disarm path in `__disarm_kprobe_ftrace()` could still invoke ftrace unregister/disarm operations even after `ftrace_kill()` had set `kprobe_ftrace_disabled`, so module unload/reload later dereferenced invalid ftrace state and crashed in `kprobes_module_callback()`.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE says “the kprobe on ftrace does not correctly handles the `kprobe_ftrace_disabled` flag set by `ftrace_kill()`,” and the patch adds an early return in `__disarm_kprobe_ftrace()` when `kprobe_ftrace_disabled` is true, with the comment “Now ftrace is disabled forever, disarm is already done.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip ftrace disarm work when kprobe ftrace has already been permanently disabled.
intent_record.what: In __disarm_kprobe_ftrace(), a new early-return check was added after lockdep_assert_held(&kprobe_mutex): if kprobe_ftrace_disabled is set, the function immediately returns 0, with a comment stating that ftrace is disabled forever and disarm has already been done.
intent_record.how: This prevents __disarm_kprobe_ftrace() from attempting to unregister ftrace callbacks when ftrace has already been permanently disabled, avoiding redundant teardown work and ensuring the function treats that state as already-disarmed.

grouping_result.intent: Skip ftrace disarm work when kprobe ftrace has already been permanently disabled.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it prevents __disarm_kprobe_ftrace() from performing ftrace unregister/disarm work after kprobe_ftrace_disabled has been set, which is the condition that led to invalid ftrace state being dereferenced during module unload/reload.

candidates.rationale: This branch unconditionally proceeds to unregister/disarm ftrace when the counter reaches 1, with no check for the permanently disabled kprobe_ftrace state. That allows disarm work to run after ftrace_kill() has invalidated ftrace state, leading to later crashes during module unload/reload.

This is the direct ftrace teardown call that becomes unsafe once kprobe_ftrace_disabled has been set. Executing it after permanent disable can dereference stale/invalid ftrace state and trigger the crash described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This branch unconditionally enters the ftrace disarm path when the counter reaches 1, without checking whether kprobe ftrace was already permanently disabled by ftrace_kill().
This is the unsafe teardown operation that can still run after permanent disable, dereferencing invalid ftrace state and contributing directly to the crash in kprobes_module_callback().
